reveal.label: Boxed warning
lines: Severe neutropenia; orthostatic hypotension, bradycardia, and syncope; seizure; myocarditis, pericarditis, and cardiomyopathy; increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis.

cards.prompt: Name the dangerous adverse effects, and how you would recognize each.

reveal.label: Dangerous adverse effects
lines: Severe neutropenia — Fever, sore throat, or other signs of infection. — Tell the senior now and get an ANC today.
Myocarditis — Early (mostly weeks 1–4): fever, tachycardia, chest pain, or flu-like illness. — Urgent troponin/CRP and EKG; escalate.
Constipation → ileus — Constipation that can progress to ileus and be fatal. — Bowel regimen is part of the prescription; ask about stools every day.
Seizures — Dose-related lowering of the seizure threshold. — Escalate any seizure; review dose and levels.

cards.prompt: Name the dangerous adverse effects, and how you would recognize each.

reveal.label: Dangerous adverse effects
lines: Lithium toxicity — Tremor, ataxia, and confusion — often when something changed (dehydration, renal function, an interacting drug). — Tell the senior now; hold the next dose and send a stat level with a BMP. Severe toxicity is a nephrology conversation (extracorporeal removal).
Teratogenicity — Ebstein anomaly risk with first-trimester exposure. — β-hCG before starting; peripartum decisions are made collaboratively, not by default discontinuation.

lines: Titrated to a 12-hour trough serum level, not to a fixed dose; draw a level about 5 days after any start or change. Confirm the dose itself with pharmacy and the current label.

reveal.label: Dangerous adverse effects
lines: Metabolic syndrome / new diabetes — Weight gain, rising glucose and lipids on the monitoring schedule. — Treat monitoring as part of the prescription; flag abnormal results on rounds.
Neuroleptic malignant syndrome — Lead-pipe rigidity, hyperthermia, and elevated CK in someone on a dopamine blocker. — Tell the senior now.

Excess sedation with parenteral benzodiazepines — Oversedation or cardiorespiratory depression when IM olanzapine is combined with a parenteral benzodiazepine. — Check the MAR for recent benzodiazepines before an IM dose.

reveal.label: Dangerous adverse effects
lines: Serotonin syndrome — Clonus, hyperreflexia, and autonomic instability with rapid onset, usually after a serotonergic agent was started or increased. — Tell the senior now; stop serotonergic agents pending evaluation.
Switch to mania in unrecognized bipolar disorder — Emerging mania or mixed features after starting. — Screen for bipolarity before the first dose.
Hyponatremia — Confusion or falls in an older adult. — Check sodium.
